subject.title: Bug: Gateway falsely marks healthy local vLLM endpoints as timed out/overloaded, causing 1–23 min fallback cascades

question: Should maintainers require a fresh current-main live vLLM timing trace before starting another fix PR for the remaining timeout cascade?
rationale: Current main fixes adjacent slices, but the central healthy-vLLM false-timeout and gateway RPC latency cascade is not isolated to one code path, so automation cannot safely choose the fix boundary from source inspection alone.

options.title: Require live trace first
options.body: Capture provider HTTP timing, idle-watchdog state, fallback decisions, auth-profile state, and gateway RPC timing on current main before approving a code fix.

options.title: Queue source-only repair
options.body: Start a fix from the most suspicious timeout path now, accepting a higher chance of patching the wrong subsystem.

options.title: Close as configuration-only
options.body: Treat current provider `timeoutSeconds` behavior as the supported solution, but only if maintainers are comfortable without reproducing the reported healthy-endpoint false timeout.

recommendation.title: Require live trace first
recommendation.body: Capture provider HTTP timing, idle-watchdog state, fallback decisions, auth-profile state, and gateway RPC timing on current main before approving a code fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is currently assigned to osolmaz and their merge history touches the closest local-provider fallback slice.
